# ASA benchmark upslope wedge, 25 Hz: transmission loss from a coupled-mode solution.
# 
# Problem: Jensen, F. B. and Ferla, C. M., "Numerical solutions of range-dependent
# benchmark problems in ocean acoustics", J. Acoust. Soc. Am. 87(4), 1499-1510 (1990);
# the same wedge is Fig. 6.8 of Jensen, Kuperman, Porter & Schmidt, Computational Ocean
# Acoustics, 2nd ed., Sect. 6.7. Isovelocity water (1500 m/s, density 1.0), depth 200 m at
# r = 0 shoaling linearly to the apex at r = 4 km; homogeneous fluid bottom 1700 m/s,
# density 1.5, 0.5 dB/wavelength; source 100 m; receivers 30 m and 150 m.
# 
# Solution: COUPLE07 (R. B. Evans, December 2007 version, distributed by OALIB as
# Modes/couple/couple07.zip), its own Test Case 2 input run unchanged: 45 modes, cylindrical
# geometry, 200 range steps across the slope, and the single-scatter matching (IOUT = -1)
# that the COUPLE documentation recommends as the verification of one-way PE models (COA
# Sect. 6.7: the backscattered field of this wedge is 40-50 dB under the outgoing one).
# COUPLE closes the bottom with a pressure-release boundary at 1500 m; the 1700 m/s sediment
# carries 0.5 dB/wavelength to 1000 m, rising to 2.5 dB/wavelength at 1500 m (an absorbing
# false bottom that stands in for the half-space). The apex depth is written as 0.01 m.
# Built with gfortran -std=legacy and stubs for the Lahey TIMER/DATE intrinsics; runtime ~30 s.
# Only this generated table is shipped: the COUPLE source carries no licence.
# 
# TL is dB re 1 m. Beyond 1.0 km the 150 m receiver lies in the sediment, and beyond
# 3.4 km the 30 m receiver does; those rows are the sediment field.
# 
# range_km  TL_30m_dB  TL_150m_dB
